title: X Thread: Water Utility Ransomware Breakdown

tweets.text: A regional water utility got hit with ransomware last month. 11 servers encrypted in under 2 hours. Billing down 4 days. But the water never stopped. Here is why. A thread.
Entry point: a maintenance contractor's login. Not rotated in 14 months. No multi-factor authentication. The attacker sat quietly for 8 days before making a move.
Then it moved fast: open-source post-exploitation tooling, straight to a domain controller, two rogue admin accounts created, network backups deleted.
What saved them: the treatment and distribution controls were on a segmented network. The malware could not cross into it. Offline backups at another site survived the deletion.
Do these this week: rotate every third-party credential, enforce MFA on remote access, isolate backups from domain admins, and rehearse cutting corporate and OT networks apart.
